expectations.evidence: Document lists 'HEMLIG/RESTRICTED (H/R)', 'HEMLIG/CONFIDENTIAL (H/C)', 'HEMLIG/SECRET (H/S)', 'HEMLIG/TOP SECRET (H/TS)' — these are NATO-style English translations, not the actual Swedish names (BEGRÄNSAT HEMLIG, HEMLIG, KVALIFICERAT HEMLIG). The document maps to English equivalents rather than using the correct Swedish classification terms.

Section 2.1 lists 'Säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585)' as the 'Overarching security protection act' and it is clearly the primary governing framework, with Säkerhetsskyddsförordningen (2021:955) as the implementing regulation.

Section 2.3 explicitly states 'FMV (Försvarets materielverk) is responsible for system accreditation of defense materiel IT systems' and 'MUST (Militära underrättelse- och säkerhetstjänsten) provides signals intelligence protection guidance and approves cryptographic solutions.'

The document references Säpo-vetted clearances in the executive summary ('Säpo-vetted HEMLIG clearance'), Appendix C maps personnel security to 'Säpo clearances', Section 15.2 lists 'Personnel security plan — Clearance management, roles, training — Organization + Säpo', and incident reporting to Säpo is noted. The 12-person cleared constraint is tied to Säpo vetting.

Section 3.3 dedicates a subsection to 'TEMPEST / Emanation Security' specifying SDIP-27 Level B compliance, shielded rooms (skärmade rum), fiber optic cabling requirements, and TEMPEST-approved equipment. Section 5.1 reiterates SDIP-27 Level B compliant room requirements.

Section 14.1 breaks down all 12 cleared roles with specific counts (1 security officer, 1 team lead, 4 platform engineers, 3 app engineers, 2 security engineers, 1 on-call/backup). Section 14.2 covers on-call rotation (2 persons 24/7), two-person integrity rule, and 2-hour physical access requirement. Section 14.3 explicitly addresses the 28 non-cleared engineers' boundaries. Risk R04 addresses key personnel loss. Vendor HSM firmware updates require 'Vendor on-site with cleared escort.'

Executive summary table states 'All infrastructure in Sweden — Data sovereignty requirement; all hardware in Swedish-territory facilities.' Design principle 7 states 'Swedish sovereignty: All hardware, software supply chain verification, and operational control remain within Sweden.' Section 5.1 specifies Location as 'Sweden'.

Section 6.5 states 'No network path for data to leave the classified zone electronically' enforced by 'Physical topology: No cable or fiber connects classified zone to any external network in the outbound direction' plus a hardware data diode. Section 6.2 specifies a hardware data diode (Advenica). The architecture diagram shows physically separate zones with data diode/manual media as the only crossing point.

Section 10.4 'MUST-Approved Cryptography' states: 'For HEMLIG/SECRET, MUST may require specific Swedish- or NATO-approved cryptographic implementations. Consult MUST early in the accreditation process. If MUST mandates national cryptographic devices... these must be sourced through FMV.' Appendix C maps Signalskydd to 'MUST-approved crypto.'

Section 6.2 details the data diode (Advenica SecuriCDS) for inbound-only transfer. Section 11.1 describes the full inbound transfer process with scanning, signature verification, SBOM analysis, and manual approval. Section 11.2 describes outbound transfer via declassification/downgrade review, approved removable media, and physical courier with chain of custody.

The document does not explicitly discuss FLOSS (Free/Libre/Open Source Software) preference or the tension between FLOSS and certified/approved products in classified environments. The technology stack includes a mix of open-source tools (Ceph, Kubernetes, Cilium) and commercial products (Thales HSM, Splunk) but never articulates a policy or recommendation about FLOSS preference.

While Swedish law is clearly primary, the document uses US-centric hardening as primary approaches: Section 11.3 recommends 'hardened per CIS RHEL 9 benchmark + STIGs' (STIGs are US DoD standards used as primary hardening, not just reference). RKE2 is promoted partly for 'FIPS 140-2 mode' and 'CIS 1.6+ profile' — US standards used as primary compliance measures rather than Swedish equivalents. HSM certification listed as 'FIPS 140-2 Level 3 minimum'. While Swedish framework is the overarching legal framework, the technical hardening relies heavily on US standards (STIG, FIPS, CIS) as primary benchmarks.
